5.5A.text: classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy of sets and subsets using graphic organizers based on their attributes and properties
5.5A.notes: Shape hierarchy (e.g., all squares are rectangles)

5.6A.text: recognize a cube with side length of one unit as a unit cube having one cubic unit of volume and the volume of a three-dimensional figure as the number of unit cubes needed to fill it with no gaps or overlaps if possible

5.6B.text: determine the volume of a rectangular prism with whole number side lengths in problems related to the number of layers times the number of unit cubes in the area of the base
5.6B.notes: Volume = layers × base area. Whole number sides. Operand maxValue=20 inferred from grade-level context, not explicit in TEKS.

5.7A.text: solve problems by calculating conversions within a measurement system, customary or metric
5.7A.notes: Unit conversion. Calculate (not just use table like Grade 4).

5.8A.text: describe the key attributes of the coordinate plane, including perpendicular number lines (axes) where the intersection (origin) of the two lines coincides with zero on each number line and the given point (0, 0); the x-coordinate, the first number in an ordered pair, indicates movement parallel to the x-axis starting at the origin; and the y-coordinate, the second number, indicates movement parallel to the y-axis starting at the origin

5.8B.text: describe the process for graphing ordered pairs of numbers in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane

5.8C.text: graph in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane ordered pairs of numbers arising from mathematical and real-world problems, including those generated by number patterns or found in an input-output table
5.8C.notes: Graphing ordered pairs - first quadrant only

5.9A.text: represent categorical data with bar graphs or frequency tables and numerical data, including data sets of measurements in fractions or decimals, with dot plots or stem-and-leaf plots

5.9B.text: represent discrete paired data on a scatterplot

5.9C.text: solve one- and two-step problems using data from a frequency table, dot plot, bar graph, stem-and-leaf plot, or scatterplot

5.10A.text: define income tax, payroll tax, sales tax, and property tax

5.10B.text: explain the difference between gross income and net income

5.10C.text: identify the advantages and disadvantages of different methods of payment, including check, credit card, debit card, and electronic payments

5.10D.text: develop a system for keeping and using financial records

5.10E.text: describe actions that might be taken to balance a budget when expenses exceed income

5.10F.notes: Balance budget - add income, subtract expenses. Financial computation.
